reflection: Volume-ratio signals (AAPL vs NVDA, z-scored) are the only consistent winners; they help RF in 2022/2023/2025 but 2024 is the persistent failure year. Close-location and QQQ volume surge help in 2023 and 2025 only. Range/ratio and gap factors fail, so I will stop those. This round I will try other normalisations of the volume ratio (rank-like, change rather than level), AAPL-vs-QQQ volume, and pair them with close-location and the QQQ trend, all of which are low-correlated with the existing factors.

lessons.name: log_aapl_msft_volume_ratio_z20
lessons.lesson: AAPL/MSFT volume ratio lacks the NVDA component (NVDA is the high-attention, high-volume stock), so it did not capture the same relative-attention signal and failed in three years.

lessons.name: log_aapl_nvda_volume_ratio_z10
lessons.lesson: A shorter 10d window is nearly a duplicate of the 20d version (0.90) and its gains come in the same years, so it mostly adds value only when paired with a different-type factor.

lessons.name: nvda_close_loc_minus_aapl_close_loc
lessons.lesson: Single-day close-location differences are noisy intraday information that hurt both models; smoothing was needed.

lessons.name: qqq_range_z20_minus_aapl_range_z20
lessons.lesson: Difference of range z-scores is noisy and collinear with existing range/volatility factors, and hurt badly in 2025.

lessons.name: aapl_range_vs_qqq_range_ratio
lessons.lesson: Ratio of ranges is unstable and overlaps with the existing range factors, giving no consistent direction.

lessons.name: aapl_gap_fill_residual_3d
lessons.lesson: Mean intraday return over 3 days is almost AAPL_mean_return_3d (0.82), so it only added noise.

factors.name: log_aapl_nvda_volume_ratio_change_5d
factors.hypothesis: The z20 level failed in 2024 perhaps because the level drifts; the 5-day change in the standardized ratio captures shifts in relative attention and is less similar to the existing level factor.

factors.name: log_aapl_qqq_volume_ratio_z20
factors.hypothesis: The AAPL-vs-NVDA volume ratio works; replacing the denominator with QQQ volume measures Apple-specific attention versus market volume and may be less regime-dependent than QQQ/MSFT.

factors.name: nvda_aapl_return_gap_vol_scaled
factors.hypothesis: NVDA's 3-day outperformance versus Apple scaled by NVDA volatility measures how stretched the leader is; Apple may catch up or reverse, and the scaling makes it comparable across regimes.

factors.name: aapl_down_day_volume_share_10d
factors.hypothesis: Volume-weighted intraday direction over 10 days measures sustained buying or selling pressure (accumulation vs distribution), which is different from return-based factors.

factors.name: qqq_close_loc_5d_mean
factors.hypothesis: Smoothed QQQ close location describes where the market is closing in its range; combined with Apple's own smoothed close location it separates market-driven from Apple-specific buying pressure.

factors.name: aapl_minus_qqq_volume_surge_gap
factors.hypothesis: Complements the AAPL/NVDA volume ratio by measuring Apple's own volume surge relative to market-wide volume surge, separating idiosyncratic from market stress.
